worldattribute-earthGlo90Download-desc:
Used by the Earth play style. Land heights come from Copernicus GLO-90 (about 90 m between points). They are kept once per machine (VintagestoryData/ModData/earth/glo90) and shared by every world and every Earth version. Sea floors, lakes and coasts are Earth's own data.

Download all (default): every square, starting when this world opens, with its progress in a window. You can play meanwhile, and stop or continue it there (.earthelevation). Earth's data release on GitHub (the default) is already converted: 8.6 GB to download and keep, a few minutes on a fast connection. Copernicus's originals are converted on this machine: about 71 GB to download, 8.6 GB kept, hours. Squares already here are skipped, so this is needed once per machine.

Download all before the world starts: the same download from Earth's data release, but a new single-player world waits for it on its loading screen, with its progress there, before any of it is made. Cancel goes back to the menu; opening the world again then plays while the rest downloads. A dedicated server downloads while it runs, as Download all does.

Download as the world reaches them: each 1° square, about 0.3 MB, when the world first needs it; Earth's included coarser GLO-90 where a square can't be had.

worldconfig-earthGlo90Download-release: Download all: Earth's data release (GitHub, 8.6 GB)

worldconfig-earthGlo90Download-copernicu: Download all: Copernicus originals (71 GB, converted here)
worldattribute-earthWorldSize-desc:
Used by the Earth play styles. The Earth's scale: at 1:10 one block is 10 m along the Equator. East-west the world holds the Equator at that scale (Cylinder World's ring, which wraps around) and 16 384 blocks of hidden seam ocean beyond each end; north-south it holds pole to pole:
1:200: 233 472 × 100 352 blocks
1:100: 433 152 × 200 192 blocks
1:50: 834 560 × 400 896 blocks
1:25: 1 635 328 × 801 280 blocks
1:10: 4 040 704 × 2 003 968 blocks
1:5: 8 047 616 × 4 007 424 blocks: the most detail, the slowest to explore and the most to store; its server needs about 7 GB of memory while it starts
Each Earth play style (Earth · 1:200 to Earth · 1:10) sets its scale with the World height and Mountain heights that suit it; changing the scale here leaves those as they are. This replaces World width and World length on the World generation tab, unless set to that tab; then make the world at least twice as wide as long (such as 1 024 000 × 512 000), or the Earth is stretched north-south. Land heights: see Terrain · GLO-90 land heights.
worldconfig-earthWorldSize-vanilla: World generation tab's width and length
worldattribute-earthSpawn-desc: Used by the Earth play style. Where new players start. Random: dry lowland anywhere on Earth whose real yearly mean temperature matches the Starting climate above, the same place for the same seed. A capital or coordinates: the nearest dry, gentle land there.
worldconfig-earthSpawn-random: Random place at the starting climate
worldattribute-earthSpawnCoordinates-des: Used by the Earth play style. Used when Start is "Coordinates below". Paste them from Google Maps: the numbers it shows when you click a place (56.949600, 24.105200), degrees, minutes and seconds (56°56'58.6"N 24°06'18.7"E), or the map's link with @latitude,longitude in it. Or type latitude, longitude in degrees, south and west negative. If they can't be read, the world starts at a random place and says why in chat.
worldattribute-earthSuezCanal-desc: Not on the world screen from Earth 2.0.1 (Suez and Panama canals there). For a server's world configuration and worlds made before: the Suez Canal on its own; on when Suez and Panama canals is off.
worldattribute-earthPanamaCanal-desc: Not on the world screen from Earth 2.0.1 (Suez and Panama canals there). For a server's world configuration and worlds made before: the Panama Canal on its own; on when Suez and Panama canals is off.
worldattribute-earthCanals-desc: Used by the Earth play style. Wide cuts at sea level for sailing: along the Suez Canal, with Lake Timsah and the Bitter Lakes, from the Mediterranean to the Red Sea; and along the Panama Canal, with lakes for Gatun and Miraflores and no locks, from the Caribbean to the Pacific. Off: the land as before the canals.
worldattribute-earthWorldHeight-desc: Used by the Earth play styles. The world height in blocks, 256 to 1024; it replaces World Height at the top of this screen. Each Earth play style sets the height for its scale, about as many metres per block up as across where that fits: 384 at 1:200 to 1:50, 512 at 1:25, 1024 at 1:10. Taller than 512: generation is slower and saves are larger. Keep Rock floor on Automatic.
worldattribute-earthRockFloor-desc: Used by the Earth play style. How far below the lowest ground in each 32 × 32 area the ground turns to plain rock, with no caves, ores or lava; the bottom layer stays mantle. A rock floor keeps tall worlds' saves small. Automatic: 160 blocks in worlds taller than 512, none otherwise.
worldattribute-earthVerticalBudget-desc: Used by the Earth play style. Blocks below sea level, independent of world height. More blocks below sea leave less room for mountains above it.
worldattribute-earthHeightCurve-desc: Used by the Earth play styles. How real elevations fit between sea level and Everest at the second-highest block. Each Earth play style sets the one for its scale: balanced relief (log 1000 m) at 1:200 to 1:50, where the world is 384 blocks high; linear (real proportions) at 1:25 and 1:10, where it is 512 or more. Linear in a lower world leaves the lowlands flat.
worldconfig-earthHeightCurve-log2000: More room for high mountains (log 2000 m)
worldattribute-earthRocks-desc: Used by the Earth play style. Vanilla (the default): the game generates its own rock layers, laid under the real ground, and Hydrate or Diedrate keeps its own aquifers. Regional: real rock regions and surface materials. Ore deposits are chosen under Ores.
worldattribute-earthOreDeposits-desc: The game places its own ore deposits, at their depth below the real ground, and Earth adds its gems (beryl, corundum, garnet, spinel, topaz, tourmaline) and ores the game doesn't place (such as chalcopyrite, tetrahedrite, wolframite and wulfenite), placed by the game's own deposit rules, in whatever rock the chosen Rocks and ground gives.
worldconfig-earthOreDeposits-vanilla: Vanilla ore deposits, plus Earth's gems and ores
worldattribute-earthSoil-desc: Used by the Earth play style. Climate only: the game's own soil from rain and warmth, as before; much of the world gets low fertility soil. Earth soil, vanilla tiers: the soil follows the real soil map, in the game's barren, low, medium and high fertility soils; barren only on inhospitable land (cold mountains, polar ground, dunes, salt). Earth soil, realistic tiers (the default): the same map in five tiers, from barren on the poorest soils (tropical red earths, sands, peat, thin soil on rock) to black earth (Terra preta) on the steppes' Chernozems. Either Earth soil leaves deserts bare, except along a river's flood (the Nile, Mesopotamia).
worldattribute-earthNature-desc: Used by the Earth play style. As around 1318: plants and animals grow and spawn where they lived around 1318, with the crops people had spread by then (olives around the Mediterranean, no maize, potatoes or tomatoes outside the Americas). Vanilla: the game, plant and animal mods place them by climate alone.
worldattribute-earthBiomes-desc: Used by the Earth play style. Earth: vegetation zones from the real climate set how dense forests and shrubs are; fire keeps the prairie, Pampas and forest-steppe open; bogs and marshes stand without trees; dry land keeps less tall grass, which greens after rain and lies flat after winter; mountains get alpine turf, fell-field and scree. Vanilla: the game's own forest and shrub maps (fed by Earth's climate) and tall grass, without these rules. Terrain, rivers, coasts, soil and rocks stay Earth's. Works with either Nature choice.
worldattribute-earthIncludeExtinctAnimal: Used by the Earth play style. Used with Plants and animals: As around 1318. Also spawns species that died out before 1318 (mammoths, cave lions, woolly rhinos) from supported animal mods. Animals still alive in 1318, such as aurochs and moa, spawn without it. Does not add animal mods.
worldattribute-earthChickensEverywhere-d: Used by the Earth play style with Plants and animals: As around 1318. On: wild chickens may spawn wherever the climate suits them, so every region has feathers for arrows. Off: chickens only where people kept them around 1318 (the Old World and Polynesia, not the Americas or Australia). With Plants and animals: Vanilla, every animal spawns by climate alone, chickens too, whatever this is set to.
worldattribute-earthRiverRapids-desc: Used by the Earth play style. Steep: white water at the drops of rivers whose real fall is strong for their size (the Congo's Livingstone rapids, Niagara, the Three Gorges, mountain rivers); between the drops, and on every other river, a gentle current. Off: no white water on river steps; waterfalls stay.
worldconfig-earthRiverRapids-steep: At the drops of steep rivers
worldattribute-earthRiverWidth-desc: Used by the Earth play style. How wide rivers are drawn, as a share of their width at 1:10. At 100 %, rivers are drawn at least as wide as boats need at 1:10 (a river of 100 m³/s 12 blocks, about 120 m), and as wide as the real river where that is wider. At a coarser scale, 100 % would make them that narrow in metres, often under a block; each Earth size therefore starts at its recommended width: 1:10 100 %, 1:25 200 %, 1:50 300 %, 1:100 500 % (a river of 100 m³/s 6 blocks, the Daugava at Riga 11, the Rhine 15), 1:200 700 %. Higher makes rivers wider, lower narrower; a river is never drawn narrower than its real width or one block, and big rivers keep their real width. If you change the Earth size, set this again (the play style for that size sets it for you).
worldattribute-earthSmallestStream-desc: Used by the Earth play style. The smallest stream drawn, by its flow. At 1:25 and 1:10 streams are drawn down to the smallest brooks, 1 m³/s, the default there; a higher value leaves out the smaller headwaters (every stream left still reaches its river), and from 20 m³/s on only the rivers' own streams remain. At 1:50 and coarser streams from this flow up to 100 m³/s are one-block streams and bigger rivers follow River width; the river data has nothing under 20 m³/s, so lower values act as 20. Each Earth size starts at its own: 1 at 1:10 and 1:25, 40 at 1:50, 100 at 1:100 and 1:200 (rivers only).
worldattribute-earthMountainSprings-desc: Used by the Earth play style. Vanilla scatters springs in stone faces and digs short streams out of mountain sides; on Earth's heights every such stream comes out as rapid water at a random spot, not where water drains. Cave springs only: vanilla's springs in cave walls below the surface, none in open cliffs and no mountain-side streams. Real stream heads: as cave springs only, plus a spring where each real stream that runs all year starts (HydroRIVERS), as rapid water where the ground below it is steep for its flow, and small springs where the ground water meets a slope in wet climates; none in deserts. Vanilla: all of them as the game makes them. Earth's rivers, lakes and waterfalls are not affected.
worldattribute-earthSurfacePonds-desc: Used by the Earth play style. Vanilla digs small ponds into the surface wherever it finds a hollow, on Earth's real ground too: round pools on hillsides and fields, and silt rings in rivers' beds. Off: none; Earth's own lakes, rivers, wetlands and the sea are not affected. Wetlands: only in the mapped bogs, marshes and swamps (GLWD v2), as often as their share of the ground. Vanilla: wherever the game makes them. Ponds in caves are the game's in every case.
worldattribute-earthElevation-desc: Used by the Earth play style; not on the Earth tab (Automatic). Where dry land's heights come from. Automatic: Copernicus GLO-90, downloaded per square, with the included GLO-90 grid where a square can't be had. worldattribute-earthWeather-desc: Used by the Earth play style. Real-climate weather: seasonal rain, storms and winds from Earth climate data. Vanilla: the game controls weather.
worldattribute-earthRainFrequency-desc: Not on the world screen (from Earth 2.0.1). Used with Earth real-climate weather: multiplies the monthly chance of rain, 0 to 3; 1 follows the real climate, 0 prevents rain. Empty: earth.json's RainFrequency (1 by default).
worldattribute-earthStormFrequency-desc: Not on the world screen (from Earth 2.0.1). Used with Earth real-climate weather: multiplies how often storms form, 0 to 5; 1 follows the real climate, 0 prevents storms. Empty: earth.json's StormFrequency (1 by default).
playstyle-desc-preset-earth: Standard survival on the real Earth at 1:100: 433 152 × 200 192 blocks, 384 blocks high, mountains in balanced relief. Real terrain, climate and native life; real rocks and ground to choose on the Earth tab. Your start is on the Player spawn and death tab, below Starting climate; the other settings are on the Earth tab, whose World height replaces the one at the top of the screen.
